title: WORK-LAB local runtime registry — which serving processes exist, how they are launched, and what they can serve
purpose: Declare the local inference runtimes once. Projects must never launch their own copy of a runtime; they call a logical provider from provider-registry.json, which maps onto a runtime declared here.

policy.noDuplicateServers: Satisfied: LM Studio is the single declared serving runtime. llama.cpp is retained as an optional, non-auto-starting escape hatch. Ollama is removed.
policy.noGlobalConfigRewrite: Starting/stopping a runtime is per-session process control; global product config is never rewritten by the model control plane.

capabilityRoles.lmstudio: Primary desktop runtime for this work package: GUI + OpenAI-compatible API on 1234 + `lms` CLI lifecycle; indexes the shared library in place.
capabilityRoles.ollama: REMOVED per user directive. Was an OpenAI-compatible model server; in 0.34.4 it stopped resolving the shared-library model root and served zero models.
capabilityRoles.llamacpp: Raw GGUF files with explicit offload control (-ngl / --n-cpu-moe), OpenAI-compatible /v1 server, precise context and KV control, and the only runtime here that serves /v1/rerank.

runtimes.endpoint_note: %USERPROFILE%\.lmstudio\.internal\http-server.json also lists a separate app-service port (observed 41343) whose /v1/models returns 404 — that is NOT the inference endpoint; the OpenAI-compatible server is 1234 after `lms server start`.

model_index.no_import_needed: Confirmed again after migration: newly placed files under <publisher>/<repo>/ were indexed automatically by `lms ls` and /api/v0/models with no `lms import` call, so no copy/move/link was performed by the tool and the single-physical-copy rule holds.
model_index.store_root_truth: MEASURED: the LM Studio model root IS the shared library root `D:\All projects\Model library` (settings.json downloadsFolder). It is scanned as <publisher>/<repo>/<file>.gguf. A probe copy placed at _idx_test_/acme/demo-repo/ was indexed as publisher=acme id=demo-repo, proving both the scan root and the layout. Because source and destination are on the same volume, migration is a same-volume move - no cross-volume link problem exists.
model_index.vision_pairing: LM Studio automatically paired Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf with mmproj-Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf from the same repo directory and reported the model as type=vlm (5.54 GB = 4.36 GB weights + 0.795 GB projector). No manual mmproj wiring was needed. This is exactly what the Ollama qwen2.5vl:7b blob could not provide.

runtimes.critical_runtime_difference: PARAMETER QUIRK IS MODEL-SPECIFIC, NOT RUNTIME-WIDE. For qwen3.5-4b this runtime IGNORES `chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false}` AND the `/no_think` prompt token (reasoning_content consumes the entire max_tokens budget, content stays empty; reproduced 3x); `reasoning_effort: "none"` DOES work. For qwen3.8-27b (DEEP) all three channels produced real content when measured on 2026-09-29. Do not generalise the 4B behaviour to other models.

model_store_defect.finding: MEASURED 2026-09-29: the running 0.34.4 server resolves OLLAMA_MODELS to the C: default `C:\Users\ALEX\.ollama\models`, NOT to the User-scope value pointing at the shared library. server.log records OLLAMA_MODELS:C:\Users\ALEX\.ollama\models and "total blobs: 0"; GET /api/tags returns {"models":[]}; `ollama list` is empty.
model_store_defect.consequence: All 5 previously pulled models (28.76 GiB of blobs in the shared library) have been invisible to Ollama since the 0.34.4 in-place upgrade, which the Inno Setup log dates to 2026-09-28 20:50:09 (/CLOSEAPPLICATIONS /FORCECLOS...), with the new server starting 20:51:06. The registry entry recorded 0.34.3 + '5 models' and was stale.
model_store_defect.impact: Ollama was serving NO models at all, so the provider bindings that pointed at :11434 (fast.legacy, code, embedding, reranker, ocr) were dead. This is why the uninstall is low-risk: it removes an installed-but-non-functional runtime.
